MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and 23 producers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: Twenty-three Moldovan wine and spirits producers will seek Chinese importers and distributors at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12.
Chinese customs data show Moldovan wine imports reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026.
About 85% of Moldova's wine production is exported, with the EU taking roughly 60% of wine exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine small formats gain traction amid moderation and single-person households
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined Australian export and domestic off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22 per cent to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39 per cent from 2023-24 to 2025-26, concentrated in Asia-Pacific markets such as Taiwan and Singapore.
Single-person households make up 26 per cent of Australian households, up from 18 per cent in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules restrict vague eco claims on wine labels from September 27
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825, known as EmpCo, bans vague environmental claims like clean, green and eco-friendly on consumer products.
Enforcement begins September 27, with national authorities setting penalties of up to four percent of annual turnover for widespread violations.
Terms like natural lack accepted definitions and are banned as generic claims unless producers substantiate them, with old stock not grandfathered.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of traded wine value as Burgundy's share jumps
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value, extending its lead on the Liv-ex market.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, while Champagne's fell from 13.0% to 8.5%.
Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive were the top-traded Burgundy producers, around a third of regional trade.

MARKET.head: India-EU trade deal to cut wine tariffs, but state rules complicate entry
MARKET.summ: For years, India has occupied a peculiar position in the international wine industry: too large to ignore, too complicated to enter
takeaways: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement will phase India's 150% tariff on EU wine down to 20% for premium and 30% for mid-range wines.
Alcohol is regulated state by state in India, so registration, taxation and distribution differ widely across regions.
India imported 5.4 million litres of wine worth US$28.8 million in 2025, up 13.7% in volume and 10.9% in value.

MARKET.head: German wine imports into China rise in volume, value and price in 2026
MARKET.summ: Imports rose in volume, value and average price in the first nine months, offering an encouraging backdrop for 45 wineries and importers heading to the German Pavilion
takeaways: China imported 4.23 million liters of bottled German wine in the first nine months of 2026, up 8% year on year.
Import value rose 11% to US$22.49 million, while the average import price increased 3%.
Germany brings 45 wineries and importers to the national pavilion at ProWine Shanghai, running Nov. 10-12.

MARKET.head: California table grapes stay available through December for holiday promotions
MARKET.summ: Despite an early start to harvest, steady shipments and cold storage supplies are in position to keep California table grapes available for holiday promotions
takeaways: California Table Grape Commission says grapes will stay in promotable volumes throughout December despite an early harvest.
Harvest is expected to end in mid-November, but shipments will continue well beyond the final picking date.
Commission research finds 72% of grape purchasers prefer U.S.-grown grapes, versus fewer than 5% preferring imports.

CULTURE.head: Brendan Carter of Bottleshock named 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year
CULTURE.summ: Last night, Brendan Carter from Bottleshock was named the 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year by Wine Communicators of Australia (WCA). The announcement was the culmination of the celebrations at WCA’s sold out annual Awards Night in Sydney, with Brendan accepting his award from WCA National Chair, Lynda Schenk.
takeaways: Wine Communicators of Australia named Brendan Carter, of Bottleshock, its 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year at its Sydney Awards Night.
Judges cited his Bottleshock.TV content and The Big Blind League wine tasting competition for engaging consumers.
Among 33 judges, 13 category winners were honoured across campaigns, digital, social media, features, packaging and events.

CULTURE.head: Stanley Wine Bar wins three awards at 2026 Tasmanian Wine List Awards
CULTURE.summ: Stanley Wine Bar has emerged as the standout of the 2026 Tasmanian Wine List of the Year Awards, taking home three major accolades, including the coveted Overall Judges' Choice Best Tasmanian Wine List of the Year. The north-west coast gem also claimed Best Small Bar Wine List and, “proving the public agrees with the experts”,...
takeaways: The 2026 Tasmanian Wine List of the Year Awards, run by Wine Tasmania, recognise venues that champion local wines.
Stanley Wine Bar on the north-west coast won Overall Judges' Choice Best Tasmanian Wine List, Best Small Bar Wine List and the People's Choice Award.
Wine Tasmania CEO Sheralee Davies said visitors travel to Tasmania for its wines and stay longer and spend more.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts her path into the American wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers hosts this VinePair Wine 101 episode, which features Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wines.
The episode is a casual conversation about how Smith Story came to work in the wine business.

CULTURE.head: Volcanic soils make wines with a distinctive tension and sense of place
CULTURE.summ:
Vines on volcanic soil are hard to grow and their grapes are hard-won, but it all combines to produce wines with a very particular sense of place

Good stories need jeopardy. Take The Princess Bride, one of my favourite films, which I recently introduced...
takeaways: Volcanic wines are a geological category rather than a style, spanning soils like ash, basalt, obsidian, pumice and tuff.
Importer Nic Rizzi of Modal Wines says volcanic wines have an extra tension that is hard to describe.
Victoria Torres Pecis farms vines on La Palma in the Canaries, including black ash soils and vines trained low against high winds.

SCIENCE.head: Barossa workshop shows reworking old-vine Grenache takes patience, not haste
SCIENCE.summ: Last Thursday, a well-attended workshop discussing and demonstrating reworking old vine Grenache was held in the Barossa Valley. Hosted by The Barossa Viticulture Technical Group (BVTG) and led by technical viticulturist Tom Bartholomaeus as well as chief viticulturist Nigel Blieschke of Torbreck Vintners, the morning led...
takeaways: The Barossa Viticulture Technical Group hosted a workshop on reworking old-vine Grenache, led by Tom Bartholomaeus and Nigel Blieschke of Torbreck Vintners.
A 2022 reworked block achieved a 75% strike rate and yielded about 1.3 tonnes per hectare less than a 2020 block at roughly 95%.
Speakers stressed slow, long-term work, and Torbreck credits keeping the same four pruners for 10 years for consistent vineyard knowledge.

SCIENCE.head: Roller-crimped cover crops improve Mediterranean vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization
SCIENCE.summ: In a 2026 study published in Field Crops Research based on Mediterranean rainfed vineyards, the authors found that roller-crimping cover crops improved soil cover, vine water status, yield (in wetter conditions), and mycorrhizal colonization without affecting grape quality, while seasonal climate was the dominant driver of...
takeaways: A 2026 Field Crops Research study of Mediterranean rainfed vineyards tested roller-crimping cover crops between vine rows.
Roller-crimping improved soil cover, vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization without affecting grape quality.
Yield rose only in wetter conditions, while seasonal climate was the dominant driver of fungal diversity.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting some Ports from Quinta do Infantado, an important Douro producer
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Infantado is a family-owned Quinta dating back to 1816. They were famous for being the first quinta to
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Quinta do Infantado, a family-owned Douro estate dating to 1816, was the first quinta to bottle Port in the region in 1979 rather than in Vila Nova de Gaia.
João Roseira heads the 46-hectare estate in Covas de Douro, with cousin Álvaro Roseira in charge of winemaking; it has farmed organically since 1990.
Graft, the estate's new UK importer, currently takes only the Ports, with Quinta do Infantado Vintage Port 2015 scored 95/100 in the tasting.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography Images: Slice of Italy
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What else do you need really? A little farmhouse, a patch of grapes, some olive trees, and the rolling hills
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: Vinography's image post features a photo of an Italian farmhouse set among grapevines, olive trees and rolling hills.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Bourgueil’s Aurélien Revillot
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Through a Burgundian lens, Cabernet Franc becomes a study of place and terroir, parcel by parcel
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Aurélien Revillot is a relatively new producer in Bourgueil whose domaine is part of Becky Wasserman's portfolio.
Revillot makes an entry-level blend from several parcels, plus single-vineyard cuvées from his best slope parcels, with two cuvées parcellaires set to join from the 2020 vintage.
Revillot, from a Mâconnais farming family, trained in Dijon and worked vintages at Domaine Drouhin in Oregon and Newton Johnson in South Africa before reaching the Loire.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós of Penedès produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872, using Spanish grapes rather than Champagne varieties.
Cava takes its name from the cellars, or caves, dug in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, where wine ages; the term became formal Spanish law in 1972.
Sumarroca Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava 2022 from Penedès, aged 40 months on lees, is priced at $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was set to visit Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but only a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain ranked sixth for value in China, below New Zealand, with per-liter value above only Chile among the top eight sources.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why I Enjoy Wine Competition Judging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Plus a guide to Le Puy wines - my notes from a recent vertical tasting
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Columnist is judging at the Asia Wine Trophy in Daejeon, South Korea, the only competition known with a dedicated orange and amber wine panel.
A Georgian Khikhvi amber received mid-90s scores from all six judges, earning instant grand gold without discussion.
Le Puy, a right-bank Bordeaux estate, left the Francs Côtes de Bordeaux appellation in 2017 and now bottles its wines as Vin de France.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Traditional labels? Suck My Duck
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Never say that wine labelling regulations are a subject devoid of humour. The Tribunal Correctionnel de Paris recently heard a case brought by anti-alcohol NGO Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over his provocative packaging. Vellas’s edgy cuvées have included “Little Fuck,” “Bad Angel” (its label...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: A Paris court heard a case by anti-alcohol group Addictions France against Languedoc vigneron Nicolas Vellas over provocative labels like "Suck My Duck".
The case tests whether such packaging breaches France's 1991 Loi Évin, which restricts alcohol advertising and bans links to social success and seduction.
Vellas's lawyer argued the labels' sexual references aimed to create a convivial environment, and the case appears adjourned for now.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The 2026 Harvest Is In , Here’s What It’s Already Telling Us About this Burgundy Wine Vintage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Early harvest data from the 2026 Burgundy vintage reveals exciting insights into the region's grapes, offering a first look at vine yields and pricing
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Burgundy's Côte d'Or picking finished between 10 and 12 September, after the region's earliest harvest ever recorded.
The Comité des Vins de Bourgogne estimates a volume drop of around 30 per cent against the five-year average, with official figures due mid-November.
Growers report small, thick-skinned berries and healthy fruit, with Côte de Beaune malic acid breaking down while tartaric acid stayed high.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says November and December bring a strong urge to cook for others, often to keep family recipes alive or try new cuisines.
The clocks drop back on Sunday, and Maker calls the stretch from then on "Kitchen Season.".
Maker shares a list of kitchen tools she uses year-round that become even more essential during festive cooking, with no affiliate links.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by Robustiano Fariña's family near O Grove, Galicia, ages magnums of its Albariño underwater in the Ría estuary.
The Attis Albariño 'Mar' is aged five months underwater at 13-16C, and is the same wine as its 'Standard' bottling, of which about 120,000 bottles are made yearly.
The author's experience with underwater-aged wines is that they generally taste tired and more advanced in age than landbound counterparts.
